title: Optimal score function estimation via derivatives constraints
abstract: arXiv:2606.19084v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We provide a statistical theory explaining why empirical score matching can achieve minimax optimal performance for diffusion generative models when the data distribution is supported on a low-dimensional manifold. More precisely, we establish convergence rates for empirical risk minimization over suitably constrained Sobolev classes and show that, under appropriate regularity conditions, the resulting score estimators lead to minimax optimal Wasserstein-1 rates for the generated distribution, up to logarithmic factors. Our results provide sufficient conditions for score-based generative modeling to generalize from the data instead of overfitting, while the resulting statistical rates depend on the intrinsic dimension of the data manifold rather than its ambient dimension.

translated_title: 通过导数约束实现最优分数函数估计
translated_abstract: 我们提供了一个统计理论，解释了当数据分布支撑在低维流形上时，经验分数匹配为何能在扩散生成模型中达到极小化极大最优性能。更准确地说，我们在适当约束的Sobolev函数类上建立了经验风险最小化的收敛速率，并证明在适当的正则性条件下，所得的分数估计器能够使生成分布达到极小化极大最优的Wasserstein-1速率（最多相差对数因子）。我们的结果为基于分数的生成建模能够从数据中泛化而非过拟合提供了充分条件，同时所得的统计速率取决于数据流形的内在维度而非其环境维度。
tldr: 该论文建立了统计理论，证明当数据分布支撑在低维流形上时，在导数约束下的经验分数匹配估计可达到极小化极大最优的收敛速率，且该速率取决于流形的内在维度而非环境维度，从而为扩散生成模型的泛化能力而非过拟合提供了理论保证。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes a statistical theory showing that, when data is supported on a low-dimensional manifold, empirical score matching under suitable derivative constraints achieves minimax optimal convergence rates that depend on the intrinsic dimension rather than the ambient dimension, providing theoretical guarantees for the generalization of diffusion generative models.
